captions.instagram:
How does a pen work?

A tiny rolling ball, a slit thinner than a hair, and ink that climbs by itself. Take apart ballpoints and fountain pens in 3D.

→ A ballpoint is just a tube of thick ink, a tiny ball, a spring and a button.
→ As it rolls, the ball picks up ink on top and lays it down underneath.
→ A bigger ball lays down a wider line.
→ Point an ordinary ballpoint at the ceiling and the ink slides away from the ball.
→ A pressurized refill pushes ink to the ball at any angle, even in space.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/penclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a pen work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A tiny rolling ball, a slit thinner than a hair, and ink that climbs by itself. Take apart ballpoints and fountain pens in 3D.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/penclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/penclear

In this video:
• A ballpoint is a ball in a socket. At the tip sits a tiny steel or tungsten-carbide ball, 0.5 to 1 mm across, held by a brass socket so it can spin but not fall out.
• Rolling carries the ink. Drag the pen and friction with the paper makes the ball roll.
• Gravity and air keep it flowing. Ordinary ballpoints need gravity to keep ink against the ball, and a tiny air hole so air can replace the ink that's used.
• Fountain pens use a split nib. A fountain pen has no ball.
• Ink out, air in. The black feed under the nib sends ink down one channel while air bubbles back up another into the reservoir.
• Capillary action does the lifting. Liquids that cling to a surface climb narrow gaps by themselves.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
